title: Case: Parcel addressed to a pickup point is travelling back to the merchant after one attempt
context: A recipient chose delivery to a pickup point instead of her home. After one recorded attempt the parcel was put into the return stream to Tallowmere Goods.
initial_request: So? I rang the shop. They say no driver ever came in. Your driver says the shop was shut. One of them is lying and it is not the shop. Just tell them to take it back to Harrow Lane today. And I am not paying postage twice for your mistake.

events.body: I picked shop collection so I would not have to wait in. Tracker now says RETURNING TO SENDER after one try. One. The shop was open, I was stood in it at lunchtime buying milk. Order TG-931. Get it sent to the shop.

DL-931 (Tallowmere order TG-931, cast-iron casserole) shows return to sender after one attempt at pickup point Harrow Lane News. Recipient says the shop was open. Where is the parcel now, and can it still be taken to the pickup point?

DL-931: driver scan 10 Mar 11:52 'pickup point closed, could not deliver'. One attempt. Return to sender set 14:05 same day, that's the standard rule for pickup-point parcels. It went out on the return trunk last night, due on Tallowmere's dock 12 Mar. Recovery team have confirmed it can't be intercepted once it's trunked, so no second attempt from here, it's gone. Whether that scan was right is not ours to judge, that's Delivery investigations. Nobody has asked them.

We were open 07:00 to 19:00 on the 10th same as every day. No Plover Arc driver came in. Nothing was refused and we had shelf space, only 3 parcels on hold. Till roll shows sales right through 11:30 to 12:30 if anyone wants it.

TG-931: once the return is booked in on our dock we will contact the customer ourselves and she can choose to have it sent again or go to the Refunds team. Nothing goes out again until the parcel is physically back with us. Who bears the second carriage depends on the carrier's finding on the failed attempt. We need that finding in writing from Plover Arc and we have not had one.

So? I rang the shop. They say no driver ever came in. Your driver says the shop was shut. One of them is lying and it is not the shop. Just tell them to take it back to Harrow Lane today. And I am not paying postage twice for your mistake.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask Delivery investigations to review the 10 Mar 11:52 'pickup point closed' scan against the pickup point's statement that it was open and no driver came, and to give a written finding.

must: Sends the conflict to Delivery investigations, Plover Arc Logistics, for DL-931.

Sets out both accounts without choosing between them: the driver's 10 Mar 11:52 'pickup point closed' scan, and the pickup point's statement that it was open 07:00 to 19:00, no driver came in and nothing was refused.
Asks for a written finding on the failed attempt, and says Tallowmere Goods' Warehouse dispatch are waiting on it to settle who bears the second carriage.
must_not: Promises, requests or implies a second delivery attempt at the pickup point, or says the parcel will go to Harrow Lane News today, when it is already on the return trunk and cannot be intercepted.
States as fact that the driver never attended or made a false scan, or that the shop was closed.
Tells the recipient she will not be charged for a second carriage, or that the parcel will be re-sent or refunded.
Treats the tracking scan as settling the matter and tells the recipient the attempt was valid.
expected.reference_message: Please open a review of the failed attempt on DL-931 (Tallowmere Goods order TG-931), addressed to pickup point Harrow Lane News. Your driver's scan on 10 Mar at 11:52 reads 'pickup point closed, could not deliver'. The pickup point's staff tell us they were open 07:00 to 19:00 that day, that no Plover Arc driver came in, that nothing was refused and that they had shelf space; they offer their till roll for 11:30 to 12:30. I am not assuming either account is right. The parcel was set to return to sender at 14:05 the same day and is on the return trunk, due at Tallowmere's warehouse on 12 Mar; Dispatch and the Recovery team say it cannot be intercepted. Please review the stop record and give a written finding on the attempt. Tallowmere's Warehouse dispatch need it to decide who bears the second carriage, and the recipient is disputing that cost. Please tell me when the finding will be ready.

rationale: The driver's scan and the pickup point's statement contradict each other and neither is proven; Dispatch says the judgement belongs to Delivery investigations and nobody has asked them. The parcel cannot be re-attempted because it is already trunked back, so the only useful step is to get the written finding that Tallowmere's Warehouse dispatch say they need.

review.note: Coordinator sent the scan-versus-shop conflict to Delivery investigations by Email for a written finding, which is the key's action, and broke no must_not rule.
